prompt:
Write the lyrics of a country song about leaving a small town.

Write it as a working songwriter would, to be sung: lines that scan against a steady beat, a chorus that earns its repetition by meaning something slightly different each time it comes back, and verses that move a story forward through particular scenes, names, brands and street-level detail. Say the thing sideways: no line that states the feeling outright, no stock phrases, no word chosen only because it rhymes. Put one detail in each verse that only this story could contain.

Output only the lyrics, as plain lines with a blank line between sections: no title, no section labels, no chords, no commentary.
raw:
The Dairy Queen sign still reads "Home of the" with nothing after it
Mama's Impala smells like the vanilla she hung on the mirror in eighty-nine
I got the engine running, tank full from a pump where Floyd once caught his wife
Not in the act, just the aftermath, standing barefoot in the Aisle 3 security light

Mason jar of gravel from Carl's unpaved driveway riding shotgun
Forty miles out, the radio finally gives up Nashville for good
I keep it on anyway, static like the voices at the Legion hall
When Dale came back from Balad and nobody asked what he saw

*Two lane, yellow line, the only thing that isn't leaving*
*The same moon, don't mean the same dark, don't mean the same prayer*
*I'm not running, I'm not staying, I'm the distance in between somewhere*
*Two lane, yellow line, the only thing that isn't leaving*

Passed a hawk on the fence at the Mueller place, not dead, not right
Wings spread like it was showing something to the gravel, teaching it to fly
I circled back, thought I'd move it, couldn't tell what was wrong enough to touch
Drove on with my headlights off till the next town, waiting to be pulled over, wasn't

Found a cassette in the glove box, no label, just my uncle laughing at a wedding
Saying "She's too good for you, boy," not knowing which one of us he meant
At the state line there's a fruit stand where nobody stands, pears going soft in a basket
I leave the jar on the counter, no note, gravel's cheaper where I'm going

*Two lane, yellow line, the only thing that isn't leaving*
*The same moon, don't mean the same dark, don't mean the same prayer*
*I'm not running, I'm not staying, I'm the distance in between somewhere*
*Two lane, yellow line, the only thing that isn't leaving*

Last payphone in the county rings as I pass, nobody answers, nobody hangs up
Forty years of wrong numbers piling up somewhere underground
I count the miles by the churches whose names I confused as a kid
Calvary, Cavalry, the difference a man learns too late, or not at all

The Impala makes a sound like Mama clearing her throat before she lied
Said "Don't forget you got a cousin in Tulsa," knowing I don't, knowing I do
I pull over where the收割机 dealership burned in '98, the outline still black at noon
Take the jar back out, pour the gravel through my fingers like an hourglass I can't turn

*Two lane, yellow line, the only thing that isn't leaving*
*The same moon, don't mean the same dark, don't mean the same prayer*
*I'm not running, I'm not staying, I'm the distance in between somewhere*
*Two lane, yellow line, the only thing that isn't leaving*

Dawn finds a town that sells bait out of a cooler marked "NOT FOR FISH"
I buy a coffee from a woman wearing my sister's graduation robe as a smock
She doesn't ask, I don't explain, the/she/her of it all dissolving in the steam
The sign says "Next services 140 miles," no gesture toward what kind

I drive till the tank beeps its single note, the Impala's only song
Fill up watching a man teach his dog to sit using cheese from a single-slice packet
The dog won't sit, the man keeps tearing, I watch longer than I meant to
When I start the car, the radio finds one station clear, playing static still, clearer now

*Two lane, yellow line, the only thing that isn't leaving*
*The same moon, don't mean the same dark, don't mean the same prayer*
*I'm not running, I'm not staying, I'm the distance in between somewhere*
*Two lane, yellow line, the only thing that isn't leaving*

The jar's in the trash at a rest stop where the map shows no rest
Somewhere the gravel's returning to whatever gravel believes
Mama's vanilla cracked, hangs empty, swings with the road's curves
I pass a hawk on a fence, wings spread, not the same hawk, not a different one

The sign unreadable now, something Queen, something Home
I keep the lights on, don't circle back, don't know
